summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would remove an outdated duplicate definition from the Customs Act, leaving the more recent definition governing advice given about export entries.
It would delete the capitalised Export entry advice definition, which predates the lower-case version introduced with earlier international trade modernisation amendments to customs legislation.
The amendment would begin on the day following royal assent and concern the terminology used in the existing customs framework for importing and exporting goods.
changes: The older capitalised definition would be repealed as redundant.
The newer lower-case definition would remain to match the export advice provision’s wording.
The repeal would take effect from the day after royal assent.
summary.affected: Exporters subject to export entry requirements would be affected.
